project.name: Awaa Braids

project.stage: MVP built: 7 milestones done; demo live, real salon connecting next
facts: Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript + Tailwind, phone first
Supabase: Postgres with Row Level Security on every table
3 roles: customer, stylist and salon admin
Booking rules enforced on the server; the database refuses double-booking
Home visits: ZIP codes 200-209 only, with travel time kept free between visits
Notifications written by the database when an appointment changes
English and Amharic; WCAG 2.1 AA checks on every main screen
Washington, DC area: US dollars and Eastern Time (daylight saving handled)
Three websites from one codebase: customers, staff, and a demo with fictional people for the portfolio

caseStudy.overview:
Braiding appointments take hours, and many braiders who work from clients' homes still book through phone calls and direct messages. Awaa Braids lets customers pick a style, see an honest price and how long it takes for the size and length they choose, request a time that is really free, and say where the stylist should come. The salon runs its day from a phone: it confirms, moves or declines requests, sees each address with a map link, manages styles, stylists, hours and the service area, and sees its numbers.

It was built in six milestones and is live with a demo anyone can try, including a one-minute guided tour.

process.intro: I started from the rules, not the screens: what a booking needs to be fair to the customer and safe for the salon, written and tested in the database first.
steps: Brief: two roles (customer and salon), the booking rules (hours, notice, cancelling, no double-booking) and a phone-first flow.
Data model and security first: Row Level Security and server-side booking, tested with database checks.
Booking in four steps, with free times worked out from hours, time off and other bookings.
The salon's tools: requests, calendar, styles and prices, working weeks and time off, reports.
Notifications from the database, Amharic, offline and accessibility checks (axe) at four widths.
Home visits: an address step, a service area by ZIP code, and travel time between visits enforced by the database.
A guided demo tour, a starter salon file and a setup guide for connecting a real salon.
The team: stylist schedules and logins, and separate websites for customers, staff and the portfolio demo.

caseStudy.problem: Booking braids by phone call or DM is slow for both sides: the price depends on size and length, a style can take four to six hours, and a stylist who travels to clients needs time between homes. Customers wait for replies and guess at prices; the salon keeps the diary and the addresses in its head or on paper and risks double-booking.

caseStudy.solution: A phone-first web app with two sides. Customers book in five steps: a style, then size and length with the price and time adding up, then a time that is really free with any stylist or a favourite, then their address, then review and send. Only ZIP codes in the service area can book, and the address is saved for next time and seen only by the customer and the salon. The salon confirms, declines or moves requests with the customer's number and a map link one tap away, sees each stylist's day and week, edits styles, prices, hours, time off and the service area, and reads simple reports. Booking runs on the server, which works out the price and time and refuses anything outside the rules, including double-booking and visits too close together to travel between. Stylists sign in on the staff website to see only their own jobs (customer, address with a map link, note, what to collect) and mark them done or missed; the admin adds them to the team, sets their hours and can remove them. Customers and staff use separate websites, and the public demo runs on fictional data with no database.

caseStudy.outcome: Seven milestones are built. The demo, with fictional people and a guided tour, is live for anyone to try, separate from the real customer and staff websites. It is checked by over 130 database checks, 95 unit tests and more than 140 browser tests at phone, tablet and laptop widths, with automatic accessibility checks (WCAG 2.1 AA) in light and dark mode. Next: connecting the real salon.
